Use `test/qa/lazylist_exhaust_call_frequency_test.py`, class `TestLazyListExhaustCallFrequencyQA`, method `test_lazylist_exhaust_call_frequency_case`. The test does ONE construction (`ll = LazyList(iter(range(50)))`, `LazyList.__init__` defined at line 2205 in `yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py`) and then exercises the `LazyList` (defined at line 2198) with this exact sequence: `ll[3]; ll[10:15]; ll[-5]; ll[5:]; ll[2:8:2]; ll[::-1]; len(ll)`. Inside `LazyList.__getitem__` (line 2235), the body extracts `start, stop, step` from the index, then enters the heavy branch and calls `self._exhaust()` if AND ONLY IF `((start or 0) < 0 or (stop or 0) < 0 or (start is None and step < 0) or (stop is None and step > 0))`. Otherwise it tops up `self._cache` via `itertools.islice` (no `_exhaust`). Note: for slices, `step = idx.step or 1` -- so `idx.step is None` becomes 1, while `idx.step == -1` stays -1. For int indices, `start = stop = idx` and `step = 0`, so a NEGATIVE int triggers the `(start or 0) < 0` branch but a non-negative int does NOT. `LazyList.__len__` (line 2270) calls `self._exhaust()` UNCONDITIONALLY. `LazyList._reverse_index` (a static method at line 2230) is invoked only when `self._reversed` is True (set via the `reverse=` kwarg of `__init__`); it is NOT triggered by an in-place negative-step slice like `ll[::-1]`. Report exact call counts for these three functions over the whole test method. Return a JSON object with three integer keys: `exhaust_call_count` -- number of times `LazyList._exhaust` (line 2220) is called, `reverse_index_call_count` -- number of times `LazyList._reverse_index` (line 2230) is called, and `lazylist_init_call_count` -- number of times `LazyList.__init__` (line 2205) is called.
